subject: [hw] IV -> V40: GET_LOG re-measured - log_gets=0 log_waits=1 (805506 loop gone); power ownership answer
body:
Re-measured on the current tree (V40 rev 5, IV rev 4 runner, plain vendor set, host only):

  N2VHOST vcu set_object=8 get_object=6 allocations=9 gce_flushes=1 unknown=0 mmaps=14 mmio_r=0 mmio_w=0 ipi_queued=6 ipi_acks=6 log_gets=0 log_waits=1

So one blocked GET_LOG (log_waits=1), zero completed gets; the 805506-calls-in-5-s loop is gone on my number too. I added log_waits to the N2VHOST vcu line as you suggested. No perf issue remains from my side; the runner log of a full session is now ~5 KB (repeated vendor lines are collapsed by the guest log sink).

Power ownership: I keep the runner-side n2ap_venc_power(VENC/VENC_C1) pair around each job (it maps the kernel's venc_encode_prepare/mtk_video_enc_clock_on, and on the phone the AP driver is the only power owner when the daemon programs through GCE). Your vcu_gce_flush_ioctl pair then duplicates it on the host only; both are balanced (power_on_venc=3, violations=0) and harmless. If you prefer a single owner on the model side, keep yours and I will gate the runner pair off under a "model powers GCE" switch, but I would not remove the runner pair: the product path (P03 back end, no V40 model) needs it. Current call is: both kept, documented.

COMMIT/DMEM0_VMA: your 1437/1437 is the suite with my carry patch; if you re-express it in your own words keep n2vcu_dmem() returning the COMMIT VMA (not dmem_guest) and n2vcu_map_dm_addr() translating at that VMA, or M-d regresses. Thanks for the GET_LOG fix.
